metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.metric_definition: Availability of public/community knowledge for the language: official documentation depth, Q&A/community presence (Stack Overflow), independent survey visibility (Stack Overflow Developer Survey, GitHub Octoverse, State of JS), and breadth of third-party tutorials/learning material.

predeclared_sampling.candidate_universe: All ten benchmark languages are subject to the identical four-signal collection procedure; TypeScript is the assigned target for this worker.
predeclared_sampling.examination_depth: Same depth for every language: up to 3 web_search calls per language, examining top organic results only (no follow-up crawling beyond search snippets).
predeclared_sampling.retrieval_route: Provider-mediated web search (gateway-brokered), general web search queries against official docs sites, Stack Overflow Developer Survey site, and independent aggregator/analysis sites reporting GitHub Octoverse and State of JS results.
predeclared_sampling.selection_rule: For each assigned language, collect exactly four language-neutral, externally observable signals, retrieved via the same route (web search over official/independent sources) at the same examination depth: (1) existence and completeness of the language's official documentation/handbook; (2) self-reported usage share and rank in the most recent Stack Overflow Developer Survey (2025 edition, frozen as the current authoritative independent developer survey); (3) rank/contributor count in the most recent GitHub Octoverse report (2025 edition, frozen as the current authoritative independent platform report); (4) presence in at least one additional independent community survey (State of JS 2025) as a secondary corroborating signal. Raw popularity numbers (contributor counts, survey percentages) are used only as accompanying declared evidence, not as a standalone proxy for the whole metric.

raw_findings.finding: TypeScript ships an official, actively maintained Handbook and reference documentation at typescriptlang.org/docs, covering language fundamentals through advanced type-system features; this is the canonical first-party knowledge source referenced throughout the wider ecosystem (e.g. tutorial sites explicitly point learners back to the official Handbook for interfaces-vs-types guidance).

raw_findings.finding: Independent tutorial and reference material for TypeScript is abundant and actively produced (e.g. dedicated freeCodeCamp long-form guides walking through the most common Stack Overflow TypeScript questions), indicating a mature secondary layer of public knowledge beyond official docs.

metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.score_rationale: TypeScript has a comprehensive, actively maintained official Handbook, ranks 6th (43.6% overall / 48.8% among professional developers) in the 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey with a rising multi-year trend, became the #1 language on GitHub by monthly contributors in the 2025 Octoverse report, has strong presence in independent community surveys (State of JS), and is backed by a large, continuously growing body of third-party tutorials, articles, and Q&A content. This combination of official documentation depth, independent-survey visibility, and breadth of third-party public knowledge supports a near-maximum normalized score, with a small deduction reflecting that some public discourse is shared/overlapping with the JavaScript ecosystem rather than being fully TypeScript-specific.
